content.sw: Katiba ya Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania, Ibara ya 11(2)–(3): kila mtu ana haki ya kupata elimu; Serikali inapaswa kujitahidi kuhakikisha fursa za kutosha na sawa za elimu na mafunzo.
content.en: Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania, Article 11(2)–(3): every person has a right to access education; the Government shall make efforts to provide equal and sufficient educational and vocational training opportunities.

source_title: Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania (official OAG English revision; consolidated through the 14th Amendment, 2005)
citation: Article 11(2)–(3), printed pages 15–16; source PDF pages 16–17
verification_note: Provision text cross-checked against the Office of the Attorney General's official English revision. This is the OAG-hosted revision consolidated through 2005, not the 2026 Constitution publication listed by NaLIS.

content.sw: Katiba, Ibara ya 12(1)–(2): binadamu wote huzaliwa huru na sawa; kila mtu anastahili heshima na kutambuliwa kwa utu wake.
content.en: Constitution, Article 12(1)–(2): all human beings are born free and equal; everyone is entitled to recognition and respect for their dignity.

source_title: Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania (official OAG English revision; consolidated through the 14th Amendment, 2005)
citation: Article 12(1)–(2), printed page 16; source PDF page 17
verification_note: Provision text cross-checked against the Office of the Attorney General's official English revision. This is the OAG-hosted revision consolidated through 2005, not the 2026 Constitution publication listed by NaLIS.

content.sw: Katiba, Ibara ya 13(1): watu wote ni sawa mbele ya sheria na wana haki ya kulindwa na kupata haki sawa bila ubaguzi.
content.en: Constitution, Article 13(1): all persons are equal before the law and are entitled, without discrimination, to protection and equality before the law.

source_title: Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania (official OAG English revision; consolidated through the 14th Amendment, 2005)
citation: Article 13(1), printed page 16; source PDF page 17
verification_note: Provision text cross-checked against the Office of the Attorney General's official English revision. This is the OAG-hosted revision consolidated through 2005, not the 2026 Constitution publication listed by NaLIS.

content.sw: Katiba, Ibara ya 14: kila mtu ana haki ya kuishi na jamii ina wajibu wa kulinda maisha yake kwa mujibu wa sheria.
content.en: Constitution, Article 14: every person has the right to live and to protection of their life by society in accordance with the law.

source_title: Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania (official OAG English revision; consolidated through the 14th Amendment, 2005)
citation: Article 14, printed page 17; source PDF page 18
verification_note: Provision text cross-checked against the Office of the Attorney General's official English revision. This is the OAG-hosted revision consolidated through 2005, not the 2026 Constitution publication listed by NaLIS.

content.sw: Katiba, Ibara ya 16(1): kila mtu anastahili kuheshimiwa na kulindwa kwa nafsi yake, faragha na usalama wake binafsi.
content.en: Constitution, Article 16(1): every person is entitled to respect and protection of their person, privacy and personal security.

source_title: Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania (official OAG English revision; consolidated through the 14th Amendment, 2005)
citation: Article 16(1), printed page 18; source PDF page 19
verification_note: Provision text cross-checked against the Office of the Attorney General's official English revision. This is the OAG-hosted revision consolidated through 2005, not the 2026 Constitution publication listed by NaLIS.

content.sw: Sheria ya Mtoto, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023, kifungu cha 8(1)–(2): wajibu wa matunzo ya mzazi au mlezi unajumuisha elimu, na mtu hapaswi kumnyima mtoto fursa ya elimu.
content.en: Law of the Child Act, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023, section 8(1)–(2): a parent's or guardian's duty to maintain a child includes education, and a person shall not deprive a child of access to education.

source_title: The Law of the Child Act, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023

content.sw: Sheria ya Mtoto, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023, kifungu cha 9(3)(a): mzazi ana wajibu wa kumlinda mtoto dhidi ya kupuuzwa, ubaguzi, ukatili, unyanyasaji, hatari za kimwili au kimaadili na ukandamizaji.
content.en: Law of the Child Act, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023, section 9(3)(a): a parent has a duty to protect a child from neglect, discrimination, violence, abuse, physical and moral hazards, and oppression.

source_title: The Law of the Child Act, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023

content.sw: Sheria ya Mtoto, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023, kifungu cha 13(1) kinakataza kumtesa mtoto au kumfanyia adhabu ya kikatili, isiyo ya kibinadamu au inayodhalilisha, ikiwemo mila inayodhalilisha au kudhuru afya ya mwili au akili. Kifungu cha 13(2) kinasema marekebisho/adhabu kwa mtoto hayawezi kuwa yasiyo na kiasi kulingana na umri na hali yake ya mwili na akili.
content.en: Law of the Child Act, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023, section 13(1) prohibits subjecting a child to torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading punishment or treatment, including a cultural practice that dehumanises or injures the child's physical or mental well-being. Section 13(2) says correction cannot be unreasonable in kind or degree considering the child's age and physical and mental condition.

source_title: The Law of the Child Act, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023

content.sw: Sheria ya Mtoto, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023, kifungu cha 160(1): mtu haruhusiwi kumfanyia mtoto ukeketaji. Kifungu cha 160(2) kinaweka adhabu ya jinai kwa ukiukaji.
content.en: Law of the Child Act, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023, section 160(1): a person shall not perform female genital mutilation on a child. Subsection 160(2) provides a criminal penalty for contravention.

source_title: The Law of the Child Act, Cap. 13 R.E. 2023

content.sw: Mwongozo na taarifa za WHO za 2025 zinasema ukeketaji hauna faida za kiafya na unaweza kudhuru afya ya mwili, akili na afya ya uzazi; madhara yanaweza kuwa ya haraka au ya muda mrefu. WHO inapinga aina zote za ukeketaji. Huu ni mwongozo wa afya wa kimataifa, si sheria ya Tanzania.
content.en: WHO's 2025 guidance and information on FGM state that it has no health benefits and can harm physical, mental and sexual health, with short- and long-term complications. WHO opposes all forms of FGM. This is international health guidance, not Tanzanian law.

source_title: WHO information on health risks of female genital mutilation
citation: Health risks of female genital mutilation (WHO)

content.sw: Msimamo wa kisheria unahitaji tahadhari: nakala rasmi ya Law of Marriage Act, Cap. 29 R.E. 2023 bado ina maandishi ya kifungu cha 13 yanayotaja miaka 18 kwa mwanaume na 15 kwa mwanamke (na mazingira ya ruhusa ya mahakama kuanzia miaka 14). Hata hivyo, katika Attorney General v Rebeca Z. Gyumi, Civil Appeal No. 204 of 2017 (Court of Appeal, 2019), Mahakama ya Rufani ilitupilia mbali rufaa ya Serikali na kuunga mkono uamuzi uliotaka umri wa miaka 18 kwa wote. Kwa sababu maandishi yaliyokusanywa na uamuzi wa mahakama havilingani wazi, usidai hapa kuwa kifungu kilibadilishwa rasmi au toa ushauri kwa shauri binafsi.
content.en: The legal position requires care: the official Law of Marriage Act, Cap. 29 R.E. 2023 text still shows section 13 ages of 18 for males and 15 for females, with possible court leave from age 14. However, in Attorney General v Rebeca Z. Gyumi, Civil Appeal No. 204 of 2017 (Court of Appeal, 2019), the Court dismissed the Government's appeal and upheld the order requiring an age of 18 for both. Because the consolidated statutory text and the court decision are not clearly reconciled here, do not claim that the Act was formally amended or give case-specific legal advice.

source_title: Law of Marriage Act, Cap. 29 R.E. 2023; Attorney General v Rebeca Z. Gyumi, Civil Appeal No. 204 of 2017 (2019)
citation: Law of Marriage Act section 13; Court of Appeal judgment, Civil Appeal No. 204 of 2017, judgment delivered 23 October 2019
